title: Transport normalization of the K-flat module derived adjunction
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $u:X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes. Put $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with $R_T$ pulled back from the point [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $P=Lu^*:D_Y\to D_X$ and $G=Ru_*:D_X\to D_Y$ be the specified total derived functors on K-flat and K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $A=D(u^*)$ be the exact termwise derived functor and $c:P\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ its canonical comparison [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. Equip $A$ with termwise shifts, $P$ with their transport along $c$, and $G$ with its fixed canonical K-injective shifts.
Let $a^P:P\dashv G$ be exactly the adjunction derived from the specified ordinary module adjunction $u^*\dashv u_*$, as in [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction, def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and let $a^A:A\dashv G$ be the canonical exact-left/K-injective-right derived adjunction of that same ordinary adjunction. Use the same right derived comparison $\beta:Q_YC(u_*)\to GQ_X$ for both, where $Q_T$ localizes cochain complexes and $C(H)$ denotes termwise application. Their left derived comparisons $\alpha^P:P Q_Y\to Q_XC(u^*)$ and $\alpha^A:A Q_Y\to Q_XC(u^*)$ obey $\alpha^A\circ cQ_Y=\alpha^P$.
Then $a^P$ is the transport of $a^A$ along $c$, with the same right adjoint and right derived comparison. Precisely, writing $\eta^P,\varepsilon^P$ and $\eta^A,\varepsilon^A$ for their units and counits, for every $M\in D_Y$ and $N\in D_X$ one has
$$\eta^P_M=G(c_M^{-1})\circ\eta^A_M,\qquad \varepsilon^P_N=\varepsilon^A_N\circ c_{GN}.$$
The unit and counit of the specified adjunction $a^P$ commute with all the fixed integer shifts; the shift on $G$ is its canonical K-injective shift, not a newly chosen adjoint shift.

proof.text: Let P be the specified K-flat left-derived pullback, A the exact termwise pullback, G the fixed K-injective pushforward, and c = modulePullbackExactComparison. The construction of c is definitionally leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Its equation leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac identifies the two left-derived counits. Apply the proved source-library tool Adjunction.derived_eq_ofNatIsoLeft to the same ordinary homotopy adjunction and the same right comparison beta. This tool uses the derived-counit normalization of lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived and right-derived uniqueness to obtain aP = aA.ofNatIsoLeft c.symm.

Evaluate this equality of adjunctions at the unit and counit components. The definition of ofNatIsoLeft gives etaP_M = etaA_M followed by G(c.inv_M), and epsilonP_N = c.hom_(GN) followed by epsilonA_N. These are precisely the two displayed formulas.

Apply canonicalRightDerivedAdjunctionShift to the specified ordinary module adjunction. It supplies CommShift for aA with the fixed K-injective shift on G. Since the published shift on P is CommShift.ofIso c.symm, Functor.CommShift.ofIso_compatibility proves that c.inv commutes with every integer shift. Adjunction.commShift_ofNatIsoLeft transports CommShift along c.symm by composition and whiskering of the unit and counit shift squares. Rewrite with the adjunction equality from step 1. This uses the existing shift on G throughout, for every integer without sign or positivity restrictions.
